text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000045 bills 99215 at about three times the complexity-adjusted expectation, with elevation in nearly every complexity tier, but the few returned charts support the billed level, so the pattern remains unresolved.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The excess is not explained by a sicker panel: the provider's 99215 share runs well above the all-provider share in every condition-count tier from 1 through 4, which is consistent with a provider-wide coding habit rather than case mix, though the share on 0-condition patients is close to peers. The documentation points the other way, but it is too thin to settle the question, since only 6 documented 99215 claims came back, all supported. Some of that support deserves scrutiny: C0022706 and C0022782 are 99215s on patients with no chronic conditions and only an upper-respiratory diagnosis (J06.9), yet they were documented as high MDM with no minutes recorded, and C0022706 is also among the notes flagged for problems. The repeated-time signal and the missing audit trail also leave open whether notes were templated or inflated to match the billed level. A reviewer should first pull the full notes for the low-complexity 99215 sample (for example C0022706, C0022782, C0022095, C0022127) to test whether the documented high MDM reflects the visit, then request a larger, targeted 99215 records sample and the EHR audit trail."}
